To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the contribution to the functional correlations in DMN is higher for the CBF than for the CMRO.

we estimated the functional correlations by means of quantitative oxygen PET using 15-O-labeled gases and H2O, and that correlation matrix derived from CBF showed larger number of brain regions compared with that derived from CMRO2, which means that CBF contributes to functional correlation in DMN more than CMRO2.
the contribution of the cerebral blood flow to the functional correlation of the default-mode networks is greater than that of cerebral metabolic rate of the oxygen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a quantitative approach to the evaluation of functional correlations in the human brain by means of PET.
the evaluation of the DMN by quantitative PET and the comparison of the contributions of CBF and the CMRO2 in the DMN.
the quantitative evaluation of the DMN by PET, and the results may contribute to understanding of the physiological basis of spontaneous activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the blood flow is a more sensitive indicator than the metabolic rate of oxygen for the functional correlation in rs-fMRI.
the CBF is a better measure for rs-fMRI than the CMRO2 in the DMN.
the CBF and the CMRO2 contribute to the DMN, and the contribution of the CMRO2 is lower than that of the CBF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DMN may be a network of the spontaneous oscillation of the regional CBF.
the BOLD rs-fMR signal is mainly driven by changes in the blood flow rather than the oxygen consumption.
the DMN is a brain network with a higher sensitivity to the regional CBF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CBF is more sensitive to the functional correlation of the DMN than the CMRO2.
the blood flow can capture the state with higher sensitivity than the oxygen consumption, which is consistent with the previous rs-fMRL study.
the BOLD signal in rs-fMRI is more influenced by the CBF than the CMRO2.
